events.label: Renault Founded
events.fact: Louis Renault and brothers founded the French automaker in Billancourt.

events.label: Ford Motor Company Founded
events.fact: Henry Ford launched the company that later introduced the Model T.

events.label: Wall Street Crash of 1929
events.fact: Major stock market collapse signaling the onset of the Great Depression.

events.label: Toyota Motor Corporation Founded
events.fact: Spun off from Toyoda Automatic Loom Works in Japan.

events.label: Hyundai Motor Company Founded
events.fact: Founded in South Korea, later expanding into a global automaker.

events.label: Microsoft Founded
events.fact: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded the software company in Albuquerque.

events.label: Amazon Founded
events.fact: Launched by Jeff Bezos as an online bookstore in Washington state.

events.label: Lehman Brothers Bankruptcy
events.fact: Peak crisis event of the global financial crash and Great Recession.

events.label: COVID-19 Market Crash
events.fact: Rapid global equity sell-off in early 2020 as pandemic lockdowns began.

events.label: Julius Caesar Assassinated
events.fact: Roman dictator assassinated on the Ides of March in Rome.

events.label: Abraham Lincoln Assassinated
events.fact: Shot at Ford's Theatre in Washington, D.C., by John Wilkes Booth.

events.label: William McKinley Assassinated
events.fact: Shot at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York.

events.label: Mona Lisa Stolen from Louvre
events.fact: Vincenzo Peruggia stole the painting, which was recovered two years later in Florence.

events.label: Mahatma Gandhi Assassinated
events.fact: Assassinated in New Delhi while holding an evening prayer meeting.

events.label: Brink's Armored Car Robbery
events.fact: Thieves stole more than $2.7 million in cash and checks in Boston.

events.label: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum Heist
events.fact: Thirteen artworks were stolen in Boston and remain unsolved.

events.label: Citizens United v. FEC
events.fact: Supreme Court ruling addressing independent political spending by corporations and unions.

events.label: Dresden Green Vault Heist
events.fact: Historic 18th-century diamond jewelry stolen from Dresden's Green Vault.

events.label: Hershey's Milk Chocolate Bar
events.fact: Milton Hershey introduced the mass-produced milk chocolate bar in the U.S..

events.label: Reese's Peanut Butter Cups Name
events.fact: H. B. Reese introduced the chocolate and peanut butter cup candy.

events.label: Dairy Queen First Store
events.fact: Soft-serve ice cream shop opened in Joliet, Illinois.

events.label: M&M's Introduced
events.fact: Sugar-coated chocolate candies debuted for U.S. military rations.

events.label: Jolly Rancher Founded
events.fact: Brand originally launched in Golden, Colorado, as an ice cream and candy shop.

events.label: Pez Candy Dispensers Marketed to Kids
events.fact: Fruit-flavored compressed sugar candies paired with character dispensers.

events.label: Pringles Debuts Nationally
events.fact: Stacked saddle-shaped potato crisps introduced in a cylindrical can.

events.label: Hot Cheetos Introduced
events.fact: Spicy chili-cheese version of Cheetos became a major snack hit.

events.label: Chipotle Founded
events.fact: Steve Ells opened the first Chipotle Mexican Grill in Denver, Colorado.

events.label: Don Quixote Part I Published
events.fact: Miguel de Cervantes published the first part of his Spanish novel.

events.label: Frankenstein Published
events.fact: Mary Shelley published her Gothic science-fiction novel.

events.label: Moby-Dick Published
events.fact: Herman Melville published his tale of Captain Ahab and the white whale.

events.label: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
events.fact: Mark Twain's novel published in the U.S. after its British release.

events.label: The Great Gatsby Published
events.fact: F. Scott Fitzgerald's Jazz Age novel set on Long Island.

events.label: Nineteen Eighty-Four Published
events.fact: George Orwell published his dystopian novel introducing "Big Brother".

events.label: To Kill a Mockingbird Published
events.fact: Harper Lee published her Pulitzer-winning novel set in Alabama.

events.label: One Hundred Years of Solitude
events.fact: Gabriel Garcia Marquez published his landmark magical realism novel.

events.label: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
events.fact: First book in J.K. Rowling's wizarding series debuted in the U.K..

events.label: A New Hope
events.fact: Original film introducing Luke Skywalker, Princess Leia, and Han Solo.

events.label: The Empire Strikes Back
events.fact: Features the Battle of Hoth and Yoda's training on Dagobah.

events.label: Return of the Jedi
events.fact: Concluded the original trilogy on the forest moon of Endor.

events.label: The Phantom Menace
events.fact: Opened the prequel trilogy with young Anakin Skywalker and pod racing.

events.label: Attack of the Clones
events.fact: Second prequel film featuring the Clone Wars beginning on Geonosis.

events.label: Revenge of the Sith
events.fact: Chronicled Anakin Skywalker's turn to Darth Vader.

events.label: The Force Awakens
events.fact: Launched the sequel trilogy with new characters Rey, Finn, and Poe.

events.label: Rogue One
events.fact: First standalone anthology film following the theft of Death Star plans.

events.label: The Rise of Skywalker
events.fact: Concluded the nine-film Skywalker saga.

events.label: The Beatles: Sgt. Pepper's
events.fact: Influential concept album featuring iconic sleeve art and studio experimentation.

events.label: Pink Floyd: The Dark Side of the Moon
events.fact: Spent hundreds of weeks on the Billboard 200 chart.

events.label: Fleetwood Mac: Rumours
events.fact: Grammy Album of the Year winner with multiple hit singles.

events.label: Michael Jackson: Thriller
events.fact: Best-selling album of all time globally.

events.label: Nirvana: Nevermind
events.fact: Propelled alternative rock and grunge into mainstream popularity.

events.label: Lauryn Hill: The Miseducation
events.fact: Acclaimed neo-soul and hip-hop album winning five Grammy Awards.

events.label: Adele: 21
events.fact: Diamond-certified album featuring "Rolling in the Deep" and "Someone like You".

events.label: Taylor Swift: 1989
events.fact: Pop transition album that won Album of the Year at the Grammys.

events.label: Beyoncé: Lemonade
events.fact: Visual album accompanying an HBO special.

events.label: Mount Tambora Eruption
events.fact: Caused global climate anomalies leading to the "Year Without a Summer".

events.label: Yellowstone National Park Established
events.fact: First national park in the United States, spanning Wyoming, Montana, and Idaho.

events.label: Yosemite National Park Established
events.fact: Protected California's Yosemite Valley and Mariposa Grove.

events.label: Kruger National Park Proclaimed
events.fact: One of Africa's largest game reserves, located in northeastern South Africa.

events.label: Passenger Pigeon Last Individual Dies
events.fact: Martha died at the Cincinnati Zoo, marking the extinction of the species.

events.label: Tasmanian Tiger Last Captive Death
events.fact: Last known thylacine died at Hobart Zoo in Tasmania.

events.label: Serengeti National Park Established
events.fact: Famous for its annual wildebeest and zebra migration in Tanzania.

events.label: Golden Toad Last Sighting
events.fact: Brightly colored amphibian of Monteverde cloud forest last seen in 1989.

events.label: Pinta Island Tortoise Lonesome George Dies
events.fact: Last known individual of the Pinta tortoise subspecies died in the Galapagos.
